purpose: Raltegravir is used to treat HIV, the virus that causes AIDS. It is used in combination with other HIV medicines to help control the virus in your body. While it does not cure HIV, it helps lower the amount of virus in your blood and keeps your immune system stronger.
how_it_works: HIV needs to insert its genetic material into your body's cells to make copies of itself and spread. Raltegravir blocks a key step in this process by stopping an enzyme called integrase, which the virus needs to do this. By blocking integrase, the medicine helps prevent the virus from multiplying and spreading in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, headache, tiredness, dizziness, and diarrhea. Some people may also notice trouble sleeping or mild stomach upset. Most side effects are mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine, as this medicine can rarely cause a serious muscle condition. Some people have experienced depression or mood changes, so let your doctor know if you feel unusually sad or have thoughts of harming yourself. Always take it with your other HIV medicines as prescribed — skipping doses can allow the virus to become resistant and harder to treat.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one 400 mg tablet twice a day, or one 600 mg tablet (Isentress HD) twice a day. It can be taken with or without food. For children, the dose depends on their weight, and it comes in different forms like chewable tablets or a powder for younger patients. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
